## Example 1.1 {#ss1-example-1-1}

Classify each sequence as finite or infinite. For each, find the 20th term, $a_{20}$:

a) $100,90,80,70,\ldots$ &nbsp; (where $a_n=110-10n$)

   - Classification: □ Finite &nbsp; □ Infinite
   - $a_{20}=$

b) $100,90,80,\ldots,-20$ &nbsp; (where $a_n=110-10n$)

   - Classification: □ Finite &nbsp; □ Infinite
   - $a_{20}=$

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 1 · Example 1.1 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
Preserve the wording, including the request for a twentieth term in (b).

(a) Infinite; a_20=110−200=−90.
(b) Finite; solve 110−10m=−20 to obtain m=13. The specified sequence has only 13 terms, so a_20 does not exist. A formula can produce an output at n=20 without that index belonging to this finite sequence.
:::
